#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "lu.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  /* not necessary for LU, but using same code as cholesky */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_lu[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
	       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j, k;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <i; j++) {
       for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
          A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
        A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
    }
   for (j = i; j < _PB_N; j++) {
       for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
          A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
    }
  }
#pragma endscop
}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_lu (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

  return 0;
}

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)          # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)          # column index
    k: dim in [0, N)          # reduction index

data:
    # A stores the matrix in-place LU factors:
    #   - unit diagonal L in the strict lower triangle (L[i,i] is implicitly 1)
    #   - U in the upper triangle including the diagonal
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # row-major

parameters:
    N: int

    # Tuning parameters for cache and SIMD usage (chosen per target machine)
    TILE_I: int  # e.g., 32   – panel height
    TILE_J: int  # e.g., 64   – width of upper update tiles
    TILE_K: int  # e.g., 32   – blocking for k-reductions

    VEC_J: int   # SIMD width along j (upper update), e.g., 8 for AVX2 double
    VEC_K: int   # SIMD width along k (reduction), often same as VEC_J
    UNROLL_K: int  # small unroll factor for k, e.g., 4

computation:
    # LU factorization without pivoting (Doolittle), in-place:
    # For each row i, first compute strict lower part L(i,0..i-1),
    # then update upper part U(i,i..N-1).

    for i in seq([0, N)):
        # ----- Strict lower triangle: compute L(i, j) for j < i -----
        # Must be sequential in j because A[i, j] depends on A[i, 0..j-1].
        for j in seq([0, i)):
            # Use a scalar accumulator to keep A[i, j] in a register.
            # This directly matches:
            #   for (k = 0; k < j; k++) A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
            #   A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
            tmp_L = A[i, j]
                    - sum(k in [0, j)) (A[i, k] * A[k, j])
            A[i, j] = tmp_L / A[j, j]

        # ----- Upper triangle including diagonal: compute U(i, j) for j >= i -----
        # Once L(i, 0..i-1) is known, each U(i, j) (j >= i) depends only on:
        #   A[i, j] (current value), A[i, 0..i-1], and A[0..i-1, j].
        # These j-iterations are mutually independent and may be parallelized.
        #
        # Mathematically:
        #   A[i, j] = A[i, j] - sum(k in [0, i)) A[i, k] * A[k, j]
        #
        # We expose this as a reduction over k and allow loop reordering.
        for j in [i, N):
            tmp_U = A[i, j]
                    - sum(k in [0, i)) (A[i, k] * A[k, j])
            A[i, j] = tmp_U


optimization:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Register reuse and reduction formulation
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # - The use of tmp_L / tmp_U expresses that A[i, j] is loaded once,
    #   updated in a register via a k-reduction, and written back once.
    # - This reduces memory traffic and makes the k loop a clear reduction,
    #   enabling vectorization and unrolling.
    #
    # (No explicit directive needed beyond the sum() notation; this is
    #  a semantic clarification of the computation.)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Blocking (tiling) for cache locality
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # We tile i, j, and k dimensions. i must remain sequential at tile level,
    # but tiling improves reuse of matrix panels/rows in caches.
    #
    # block(DIMENSION, TILE_DIMENSION, TILE_SIZE) splits:
    #   DIMENSION = TILE_DIMENSION * TILE_SIZE + inner_remainder
    # and nests loops as for TILE_DIMENSION (outer) and DIMENSION (inner).

    block(i, I, TILE_I)   # panel/blocking over rows
    block(j, J, TILE_J)   # tiling over columns, mainly effective for U-part
    block(k, K, TILE_K)   # tiling the reduction to fit A[*][k] and A[k][*] in cache

    # Keep I (the tile index of i) at the outermost level to preserve
    # row-wise dependency ordering: earlier i-tiles complete before later ones.
    hoist(I)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Loop interchange in the upper update (rank-1 style update)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # For the upper-part update, a more cache-friendly form is:
    #   for i:
    #     for k in [0, i):
    #       let lik = A[i, k];
    #       for j in [i, N):
    #         A[i, j] -= lik * A[k, j];
    #
    # This reuses A[i, k] across all j and expresses a sequence of rank-1
    # updates. It is obtained by interchanging j and k in the U loop
    # (and hoisting A[i, k] into a scalar), which is mathematically
    # equivalent to the sum-reduction formulation above.

    #interchange(J, K)  # applied only in the U(i, j) computation region
    #hoist(A[i, K])     # keep A[i, k] (lik) in a scalar across inner j-loop

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Parallelism
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # - The outer i-dimension cannot be parallelized due to true dependencies:
    #   row i uses factors from rows 0..i-1.
    # - Within a given i:
    #   * The lower-part (j < i) is strictly sequential in j.
    #   * The upper-part (j >= i) is embarrassingly parallel across j
    #     once the entire lower row i is computed.

    # Parallelize the j-dimension only for the upper update loop.
    # This assumes a code generator capable of distinguishing the
    # j-loop region with j in [i, N).
    parallelize(j)  # in the upper-triangular (U) update region only

    # Optionally, when using the interchanged U loop:
    #   parallelize(J)  # outer j-tiles, so each thread updates a stripe of columns

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Vectorization and unrolling of reductions
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # - The k-reductions for both L and U updates are good SIMD candidates:
    #   contiguous access to either A[i, k] (row) or A[k, j] (column)
    #   depending on interchange decisions and architecture.
    # - We vectorize K (inner blocked k) and unroll it to reduce loop overhead.

    vectorize(K, VEC_K)     # vectorize inner k-block in reductions
    unroll(K, UNROLL_K)     # unroll reduction loop for better ILP

    # In the U(i, j) loop before interchange (original j-outer, k-inner form),
    # vectorizing j instead can also be beneficial when TILE_J is large enough.
    vectorize(J, VEC_J)     # SIMD across columns in upper update

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Summary of data-layout decision
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # We retain row-major layout:
    #   - Access A[i, k] with unit stride in the innermost k-loop
    #     (original form) or second-innermost loop (after interchange).
    #   - Access A[k, j] with stride N, but blocking over k and j mitigates this.
    #
    # Changing A to column-major would only swap which of A[i, k] or A[k, j]
    # is contiguous and would complicate interoperability; given the strong
    # reuse of row i in each iteration and the in-place nature of LU,
    # we keep the original row-major layout.
--- END OF MODEL: lu-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: lu-02 ---
domain:
    # Matrix dimension
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, N)
    t: dim in [0, N)  # used for Gram-matrix construction in init_array

data:
    # Global matrix A: initialized in init_array, factorized in-place by kernel_lu
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

    # Temporary matrix used only inside init_array to build a Gram matrix
    B[i, j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

parameters:
    N: int  # problem size

    # Tuning parameters (constants chosen for a given machine)
    TJ_init:   int  # tile size in j for Gram-matrix construction
    TT_init:   int  # tile size in t for Gram-matrix construction
    TI_init:   int  # tile size in i for Gram-matrix construction

    TJ_lu:     int  # tile size along j in the LU trailing-update
    VECW:      int  # vector width for j-vectorization (e.g., 4 for AVX2 double)
    UNROLL_K:  int  # unroll factor for k-loop inside LU (e.g., 2–4)


computation:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. init_array: build initial lower-triangular A and then
    #    replace it by a symmetric positive semi-definite A := A * A^T
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1.a Seed A as a unit-lower-triangular-like matrix
    init_lower:
      for i in [0, N), j in [0, i]:
        A[i, j] = (DATA_TYPE)((-j % N)) / N + (DATA_TYPE)1

    init_upper:
      for i in [0, N), j in (i, N):
        A[i, j] = (DATA_TYPE)0

    init_diag:
      for i in [0, N):
        A[i, i] = (DATA_TYPE)1

    # 1.b Build B = A * A^T (Gram matrix), then A := B.
    #     This is exactly what the nested loops over t, r, s compute.

    zero_B:
      for i, j:
        B[i, j] = (DATA_TYPE)0

    gram_B:
      # B[i, j] = sum_t A[i, t] * A[j, t]
      for i, j:
        B[i, j] = sum(t in [0, N), A[i, t] * A[j, t])

    copy_B_to_A:
      for i, j:
        A[i, j] = B[i, j]


    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. kernel_lu: in-place LU factorization without pivoting
    #
    # Original kernel:
    #   for i = 0..N-1:
    #     # L-row
    #     for j = 0..i-1:
    #       for k = 0..j-1:
    #         A[i,j] -= A[i,k] * A[k,j];
    #       A[i,j] /= A[j,j];
    #     # U-row
    #     for j = i..N-1:
    #       for k = 0..i-1:
    #         A[i,j] -= A[i,k] * A[k,j];
    #
    # Below we express an equivalent right-looking formulation that
    # preserves the per-element operation order and thus the bitwise
    # result, but has better locality and vectorization properties.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    LU_factor:
      # i is sequential: each row depends on rows 0..i-1
      for i in seq(0, N):

        # For each previous column k of row i:
        for k in seq(0, i):
          # 2.a Compute one L(i, k) entry in the strictly lower part.
          #     For k == i, this is skipped; unit diagonal is implicit.
          if k < i:
            # At this point A[i, k] already contains
            #   A[i, k]_0 - sum_{p=0..k-1} L(i, p) * U(p, k)
            # so the division produces L(i, k).
            A[i, k] = A[i, k] / A[k, k]

          # 2.b Right-looking update of the trailing part of row i:
          #     for all columns j > k, subtract the k-th rank-1 contribution.
          #     This covers:
          #       - j in (k, i): remaining L(i, j) numerators
          #       - j in [i, N): U(i, j) entries.
          for j in (k + 1, N):
            # A[i, j] -= L(i, k) * U(k, j)
            # where L(i, k) is now stored in A[i, k] and U(k, j) in A[k, j].
            A[i, j] = A[i, j] - A[i, k] * A[k, j]


dependencies:
    # Explicitly describe key dependencies for the LU factorization.

    # (1) Row-wise dependency: to factor row i, all rows < i must be complete
    #     (both their L and U parts), since they are used as U(k, *) and
    #     L(*, k) in later rows.
    for i in [1, N):
      LU_factor(i - 1) -> LU_factor(i)

    # (2) Within row i, each step k depends on all previous k' < k
    #     because A[i, k] uses updated values A[i, p] with p < k and
    #     U(p, k) from earlier rows.
    for i in [0, N), k in [1, i):
      LU_factor(i, k - 1) -> LU_factor(i, k)


optimization:
    # ============================================================
    # Optimizations for init_array (Gram matrix A := A * A^T)
    # ============================================================

    # Recognize gram_B as B = A * A^T and turn it into a cache-blocked GEMM.
    block(i, I_init, TI_init)   # tile rows of B
    block(j, J_init, TJ_init)   # tile columns of B
    block(t, T_init, TT_init)   # tile inner-product dimension

    # Within each (I_init, J_init, T_init) tile, the computation becomes:
    #   for i in I_init:
    #     for j in J_init:
    #       B[i, j] += sum_{t in T_init} A[i, t] * A[j, t]
    # which has good temporal locality for tiles of A and B.

    # Exploit symmetry of B = A * A^T to cut work almost in half.
    # This is semantics-preserving and bitwise identical because
    #   B[i, j] and B[j, i] are computed as the same sum of the same
    #   products in the same order in the original code.
    #
    # We express this as:
    #   - Restrict gram_B to i <= j (upper triangle including diagonal).
    #   - Add a symmetric fill step for the lower triangle.
    #
    # #symmetric_half_gram:
    #   for i in [0, N), j in [i, N):
    #     B[i, j] = sum(t, A[i, t] * A[j, t])
    #   for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
    #     B[i, j] = B[j, i]

    parallelize(I_init)         # distribute row-tiles of B across cores
    vectorize(j, VECW)          # vectorize across columns inside a tile


    # ============================================================
    # Optimizations for kernel_lu (in-place LU)
    # ============================================================

    # Keep i as the outermost sequential loop (strong inter-row deps).
    hoist(i)

    # The LU_factor computation already encodes a right-looking form
    # derived from the original two nested loops via legal transforms:
    #
    #  - For the original U-update (second j-loop), we interchange (j, k):
    #       for j = i..N-1
    #         for k = 0..i-1   body(i,j,k)
    #    ->  for k = 0..i-1
    #         for j = i..N-1   body(i,j,k)
    #    This preserves the order of updates for each (i, j) element,
    #    so floating-point results are bitwise identical.
    #
    #  - For the L-update (first j-loop), we similarly transform the
    #    left-looking scheme into an equivalent right-looking one:
    #       for j = 0..i-1:
    #         for k = 0..j-1: A[i,j] -= A[i,k]*A[k,j];
    #         A[i,j] /= A[j,j];
    #    ->
    #       for k = 0..i-1:
    #         A[i,k] /= A[k,k];
    #         for j = k+1..i-1: A[i,j] -= A[i,k]*A[k,j];
    #    Again, the sequence of operations on each A[i,j] is unchanged.

    # Improve locality and vectorization in the trailing update (inner j-loop).
    block(j, J_lu, TJ_lu)       # work on tiles along the row (j dimension)
    hoist(J_lu)

    # For a fixed (i, k), each j-tile J_lu touches a contiguous segment
    # of rows i and k, ideal for cache lines and SIMD.

    # Parallelize across independent j-tiles within each row i.
    # Each tile updates a disjoint interval of row i and only reads
    # shared, read-only data from previous rows, so no synchronization
    # is needed beyond the natural barrier at each i.
    parallelize(J_lu)

    # Vectorize inside j-tiles: the inner loop becomes a SAXPY-like
    # fused multiply-subtract on contiguous memory (A[k, j], A[i, j]).
    vectorize(j, VECW)

    # Unroll k to increase instruction-level parallelism in the chain
    # over previous columns while keeping code size reasonable.
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)

    # Implicit scalar/temporal hoisting (captured by the loop form):
    #   - A[i, k] is loaded once per (i, k), kept in a scalar register
    #   - A[k, j] is streamed contiguously inside each tile
    #   - A[i, j] is accumulated in registers across k and written back once
--- END OF MODEL: lu-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: lu-03 ---
domain:
    # Matrix is N x N, 0-based as in the C code
    i:  dim in [0, N)      # row index
    jL: dim in [0, N)      # column index for L-part (j < i)
    jU: dim in [0, N)      # column index for U-part (j >= i)
    k:  dim in [0, N)      # reduction / inner-product index

data:
    # In-place LU factors, stored in a single row-major array:
    #   - strict lower triangle (i > j): L (unit diagonal implied)
    #   - upper triangle (i <= j): U
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major layout

parameters:
    N: int                    # problem size
    # Tuning knobs for performance (compile-time or run-time constants):
    TJ: int                   # tile size for jU (columns of trailing submatrix), e.g., 64–256
    TK: int                   # tile size for k in U-part, e.g., 16–64
    TK_L: int                 # tile size for k in L-part, typically smaller than TK
    VJ: int                   # SIMD width used for vectorizing over columns (jU)
    UK: int                   # unroll factor for K in U-part
    UK_L: int                 # unroll factor for K in L-part

computation:
    # For each row i, first compute L(i, j) for j < i, then U(i, j) for j >= i.
    # This matches the original kernel_lu loop nest structurally.

    for i in seq([0, N)):

        # --- L update: strict lower triangle, row i, columns 0 .. i-1 ---
        # A[i, jL] = ( A[i, jL] - sum_{k=0}^{jL-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jL] ) / A[jL, jL]
        # jL must be processed in increasing order because A[i, k] for k < jL
        # are produced by earlier jL iterations.
        L(i, jL):
            for jL in seq([0, i)):
                A[i, jL] =
                    ( A[i, jL]
                      - sum(k in [0, jL): A[i, k] * A[k, jL] )
                    ) / A[jL, jL]

        # --- U update: upper triangle including diagonal, row i, columns i .. N-1 ---
        # A[i, jU] = A[i, jU] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jU]
        # For fixed i, different jU iterations are independent.
        U(i, jU):
            for jU in [i, N):
                A[i, jU] =
                    A[i, jU]
                    - sum(k in [0, i): A[i, k] * A[k, jU])

dependencies:
    # The row loop i is explicitly sequential (seq), so rows execute in order:
    #   all updates for row i happen before row i+1.
    #
    # Within each row i:
    #   - L(i, jL) is sequential in jL by construction (seq).
    #   - U(i, jU) is independent across jU once all L(i, *) are known.
    #
    # To make this explicit:
    for i in [0, N), jL in [0, i), jU in [i, N):
        L(i, jL) -> U(i, jU)   # complete the L-part of row i before any U-part of row i

optimization:
    # High-level goals:
    #   - Respect all true data dependencies (no pivoting is introduced).
    #   - Keep the lower-triangular (L) jL-loop strictly sequential.
    #   - Turn the U-part into a cache-friendly, vectorized, and parallel update
    #     over the trailing submatrix.

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Reorder the U update to improve reuse (saxpy-like formulation)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # U(i, jU) currently computes:
    #   A[i, jU] = A[i, jU] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jU]
    # which is mathematically a reduction over k. The contributions from
    # different k are associative (up to FP round-off), so we can swap jU and k.
    #
    # Conceptual transformed order for the U-part at fixed i:
    #   for k in [0, i):
    #       let aik = A[i, k]    # hoist to a scalar
    #       for jU in [i, N):
    #           A[i, jU] -= aik * A[k, jU]
    #
    # This:
    #   - keeps A[i, k] (aik) in a register across many jU,
    #   - streams A[k, jU] and A[i, jU] in contiguous row-major order,
    #   - preserves the mathematical result.
    #
    # We express this via an interchange of jU and k in the U reduction.
    # (L's use of k is unchanged.)
    interchange(jU, k)  # applied only where jU and k are both active, effectively in U

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Tiling / blocking of U’s jU and k dimensions
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # After reordering, U’s effective structure per row i is:
    #   for k in [0, i):
    #     for jU in [i, N):
    #       A[i, jU] -= A[i, k] * A[k, jU]
    #
    # We tile jU and k to form cache-sized blocks over the trailing submatrix.
    # TJ and TK are tunable tile sizes that should be chosen to fit L1/L2.
    block(jU, JU, TJ)   # tile the trailing columns for better spatial locality

    j: dim in [0, N)

    # On input: arbitrary SPD matrix A.
    # On output: in-place LU factorization without pivoting:
    #   - L has unit diagonal and is stored in the strict lower triangle of A.
    #   - U is stored in the diagonal and upper triangle of A.

    # Problem size (matches PolyBench's N and _PB_N)
    N: int

    TJ: int  # tile size for column dimension in upper update, e.g., 64
    UK: int  # unroll factor for inner products over k, e.g., 4
    VLEN: int  # SIMD width (number of DATA_TYPE lanes), e.g., 4 or 8

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # This is a Doolittle-like algorithm:
    #   For each row i:
    #     1) Compute L[i, 0..i-1] (strict lower part of row i).
    #     2) Compute U[i, i..N-1] (diagonal and upper part of row i).
    #
    # The original C code:
    #   for (i)
    #     for (j < i) { for (k < j) A[i][j] -= A[i][k]*A[k][j]; A[i][j] /= A[j][j]; }
    #     for (j >= i) for (k < i) A[i][j] -= A[i][k]*A[k][j];

    for i in seq([0, N)):                # outer loop must be sequential (row-to-row dependence)

        # 1) Compute strict lower part of row i: L(i, j) for j < i.
        #    Each A[i, j] is updated as:
        #       A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - sum_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i, k] * A[k, j]) / A[j, j]
        #    Note that A[i, k] for k < j are entries of L in row i, so j must be
        #    processed in increasing order (loop-carried dependence on row i).
        for j in seq([0, i)):
            A[i, j] =
                ( A[i, j]
                  - sum(k in [0, j), A[i, k] * A[k, j]) )
                / A[j, j]

        # 2) Compute diagonal and upper part of row i: U(i, j) for j >= i.
        #    Each A[i, j] is updated as:
        #       A[i, j] = A[i, j] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[k, j]
        #    All A[i, k] with k < i are now fixed (L row i is complete), and all
        #    A[k, j] with k < i, j >= i are from previously computed rows.

        #      - the sum over k is a pure reduction for each (i, j).

                - sum(k in [0, i), A[i, k] * A[k, j])

    # Row dependencies:
    #   All computations at row i depend on rows 0..i-1.
    #   This enforces that i must be executed sequentially.

    #   - The lower-triangular loop over j (j < i) is also sequential because
    #     L(i, j) uses previously computed L(i, k) with k < j.
    #   - The upper-triangular loop (j >= i) has no loop-carried dependencies

    # (we do not interchange j and k), therefore preserving C’s semantics for

    #   for JU in [i, N) step TJ:

    hoist(JU)

    vectorize(j, VLEN)

    # We unroll and vectorize k to extract ILP and exploit SIMD where possible.

    vectorize(k, VLEN)

    # but can reduce working-set size for large N by grouping nearby rows.
    # The transformation is:

    # into:

    #     for i in [I, min(I+TI, N)):
    #       ...

    #   hoist(I)

/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  /* not necessary for LU, but using same code as cholesky */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_lu[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
	       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j, k;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <i; j++) {
       for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
          A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
        A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
    }
   for (j = i; j < _PB_N; j++) {
       for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
          A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
    }
  }
#pragma endscop
}

{

  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_lu (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed

  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

  return 0;
}

    #       let lik = A[i, k];
    #       for j in [i, N):
    #         A[i, j] -= lik * A[k, j];
    #
    # This reuses A[i, k] across all j and expresses a sequence of rank-1
    # updates. It is obtained by interchanging j and k in the U loop
    # (and hoisting A[i, k] into a scalar), which is mathematically
    # equivalent to the sum-reduction formulation above.

    #interchange(J, K)  # applied only in the U(i, j) computation region
    #hoist(A[i, K])     # keep A[i, k] (lik) in a scalar across inner j-loop

    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    #   row i uses factors from rows 0..i-1.
    # - Within a given i:

    #   * The upper-part (j >= i) is embarrassingly parallel across j
    #     once the entire lower row i is computed.

    # Parallelize the j-dimension only for the upper update loop.
    # This assumes a code generator capable of distinguishing the
    # j-loop region with j in [i, N).
    parallelize(j)  # in the upper-triangular (U) update region only

    # Optionally, when using the interchanged U loop:
    #   parallelize(J)  # outer j-tiles, so each thread updates a stripe of columns

    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    #   contiguous access to either A[i, k] (row) or A[k, j] (column)
    #   depending on interchange decisions and architecture.
    # - We vectorize K (inner blocked k) and unroll it to reduce loop overhead.

    vectorize(K, VEC_K)     # vectorize inner k-block in reductions
    unroll(K, UNROLL_K)     # unroll reduction loop for better ILP

    # vectorizing j instead can also be beneficial when TILE_J is large enough.
    vectorize(J, VEC_J)     # SIMD across columns in upper update

    # 6. Summary of data-layout decision
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # We retain row-major layout:
    #   - Access A[i, k] with unit stride in the innermost k-loop
    #     (original form) or second-innermost loop (after interchange).
    #   - Access A[k, j] with stride N, but blocking over k and j mitigates this.

    # Changing A to column-major would only swap which of A[i, k] or A[k, j]
    # is contiguous and would complicate interoperability; given the strong
    # reuse of row i in each iteration and the in-place nature of LU,
    # we keep the original row-major layout.

parameters:
    N: int  # problem size

computation:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. init_array: build initial lower-triangular A and then
    #    replace it by a symmetric positive semi-definite A := A * A^T
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1.a Seed A as a unit-lower-triangular-like matrix
    init_lower:
      for i in [0, N), j in [0, i]:
        A[i, j] = (DATA_TYPE)((-j % N)) / N + (DATA_TYPE)1

    init_upper:
      for i in [0, N), j in (i, N):
        A[i, j] = (DATA_TYPE)0

    init_diag:
      for i in [0, N):
        A[i, i] = (DATA_TYPE)1

    # 1.b Build B = A * A^T (Gram matrix), then A := B.
    #     This is exactly what the nested loops over t, r, s compute.

    zero_B:
      for i, j:
        B[i, j] = (DATA_TYPE)0

    gram_B:
      # B[i, j] = sum_t A[i, t] * A[j, t]
      for i, j:
        B[i, j] = sum(t in [0, N), A[i, t] * A[j, t])

    copy_B_to_A:
      for i, j:
        A[i, j] = B[i, j]


    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. kernel_lu: in-place LU factorization without pivoting
    #
    # Original kernel:
    #   for i = 0..N-1:
    #     # L-row
    #     for j = 0..i-1:
    #       for k = 0..j-1:
    #         A[i,j] -= A[i,k] * A[k,j];
    #       A[i,j] /= A[j,j];
    #     # U-row
    #     for j = i..N-1:
    #       for k = 0..i-1:
    #         A[i,j] -= A[i,k] * A[k,j];
    #
    # Below we express an equivalent right-looking formulation that
    # preserves the per-element operation order and thus the bitwise
    # result, but has better locality and vectorization properties.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    LU_factor:
      # i is sequential: each row depends on rows 0..i-1
      for i in seq(0, N):

        # For each previous column k of row i:
        for k in seq(0, i):
          # 2.a Compute one L(i, k) entry in the strictly lower part.
          #     For k == i, this is skipped; unit diagonal is implicit.
          if k < i:
            # At this point A[i, k] already contains
            #   A[i, k]_0 - sum_{p=0..k-1} L(i, p) * U(p, k)
            # so the division produces L(i, k).
            A[i, k] = A[i, k] / A[k, k]

          # 2.b Right-looking update of the trailing part of row i:
          #     for all columns j > k, subtract the k-th rank-1 contribution.
          #     This covers:
          #       - j in (k, i): remaining L(i, j) numerators
          #       - j in [i, N): U(i, j) entries.
          for j in (k + 1, N):
            # A[i, j] -= L(i, k) * U(k, j)
            # where L(i, k) is now stored in A[i, k] and U(k, j) in A[k, j].
            A[i, j] = A[i, j] - A[i, k] * A[k, j]


dependencies:
    # Explicitly describe key dependencies for the LU factorization.

    # (1) Row-wise dependency: to factor row i, all rows < i must be complete
    #     (both their L and U parts), since they are used as U(k, *) and
    #     L(*, k) in later rows.
    for i in [1, N):
      LU_factor(i - 1) -> LU_factor(i)

    # (2) Within row i, each step k depends on all previous k' < k
    #     because A[i, k] uses updated values A[i, p] with p < k and
    #     U(p, k) from earlier rows.
    for i in [0, N), k in [1, i):
      LU_factor(i, k - 1) -> LU_factor(i, k)


optimization:
    # ============================================================
    # Optimizations for init_array (Gram matrix A := A * A^T)
    # ============================================================

    # Recognize gram_B as B = A * A^T and turn it into a cache-blocked GEMM.
    block(i, I_init, TI_init)   # tile rows of B
    block(j, J_init, TJ_init)   # tile columns of B
    block(t, T_init, TT_init)   # tile inner-product dimension

    # Within each (I_init, J_init, T_init) tile, the computation becomes:
    #   for i in I_init:
    #     for j in J_init:
    #       B[i, j] += sum_{t in T_init} A[i, t] * A[j, t]
    # which has good temporal locality for tiles of A and B.

    # Exploit symmetry of B = A * A^T to cut work almost in half.
    # This is semantics-preserving and bitwise identical because
    #   B[i, j] and B[j, i] are computed as the same sum of the same
    #   products in the same order in the original code.
    #
    # We express this as:
    #   - Restrict gram_B to i <= j (upper triangle including diagonal).
    #   - Add a symmetric fill step for the lower triangle.
    #
    # #symmetric_half_gram:
    #   for i in [0, N), j in [i, N):
    #     B[i, j] = sum(t, A[i, t] * A[j, t])
    #   for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
    #     B[i, j] = B[j, i]

    parallelize(I_init)         # distribute row-tiles of B across cores
    vectorize(j, VECW)          # vectorize across columns inside a tile


    # ============================================================
    # Optimizations for kernel_lu (in-place LU)
    # ============================================================

    # Keep i as the outermost sequential loop (strong inter-row deps).
    hoist(i)

    # The LU_factor computation already encodes a right-looking form
    # derived from the original two nested loops via legal transforms:
    #
    #  - For the original U-update (second j-loop), we interchange (j, k):
    #       for j = i..N-1
    #         for k = 0..i-1   body(i,j,k)
    #    ->  for k = 0..i-1
    #         for j = i..N-1   body(i,j,k)
    #    This preserves the order of updates for each (i, j) element,
    #    so floating-point results are bitwise identical.
    #
    #  - For the L-update (first j-loop), we similarly transform the
    #    left-looking scheme into an equivalent right-looking one:
    #       for j = 0..i-1:
    #         for k = 0..j-1: A[i,j] -= A[i,k]*A[k,j];
    #         A[i,j] /= A[j,j];
    #    ->
    #       for k = 0..i-1:
    #         A[i,k] /= A[k,k];
    #         for j = k+1..i-1: A[i,j] -= A[i,k]*A[k,j];
    #    Again, the sequence of operations on each A[i,j] is unchanged.

    # Improve locality and vectorization in the trailing update (inner j-loop).
    block(j, J_lu, TJ_lu)       # work on tiles along the row (j dimension)
    hoist(J_lu)

    # For a fixed (i, k), each j-tile J_lu touches a contiguous segment
    # of rows i and k, ideal for cache lines and SIMD.

    # Parallelize across independent j-tiles within each row i.
    # Each tile updates a disjoint interval of row i and only reads
    # shared, read-only data from previous rows, so no synchronization
    # is needed beyond the natural barrier at each i.
    parallelize(J_lu)

    # Vectorize inside j-tiles: the inner loop becomes a SAXPY-like
    # fused multiply-subtract on contiguous memory (A[k, j], A[i, j]).
    vectorize(j, VECW)

    # Unroll k to increase instruction-level parallelism in the chain
    # over previous columns while keeping code size reasonable.
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)

    # Implicit scalar/temporal hoisting (captured by the loop form):
    #   - A[i, k] is loaded once per (i, k), kept in a scalar register
    #   - A[k, j] is streamed contiguously inside each tile
    #   - A[i, j] is accumulated in registers across k and written back once
--- END OF MODEL: lu-02 ---

    jU: dim in [0, N)      # column index for U-part (j >= i)
    k:  dim in [0, N)      # reduction / inner-product index

    # In-place LU factors, stored in a single row-major array:
    #   - strict lower triangle (i > j): L (unit diagonal implied)
    #   - upper triangle (i <= j): U
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major layout

parameters:
    N: int                    # problem size
    # Tuning knobs for performance (compile-time or run-time constants):
    TJ: int                   # tile size for jU (columns of trailing submatrix), e.g., 64–256
    TK: int                   # tile size for k in U-part, e.g., 16–64
    TK_L: int                 # tile size for k in L-part, typically smaller than TK
    VJ: int                   # SIMD width used for vectorizing over columns (jU)
    UK: int                   # unroll factor for K in U-part
    UK_L: int                 # unroll factor for K in L-part

computation:
    # For each row i, first compute L(i, j) for j < i, then U(i, j) for j >= i.
    # This matches the original kernel_lu loop nest structurally.

    for i in seq([0, N)):

        # --- L update: strict lower triangle, row i, columns 0 .. i-1 ---
        # A[i, jL] = ( A[i, jL] - sum_{k=0}^{jL-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jL] ) / A[jL, jL]
        # jL must be processed in increasing order because A[i, k] for k < jL
        # are produced by earlier jL iterations.
        L(i, jL):
            for jL in seq([0, i)):
                A[i, jL] =
                    ( A[i, jL]
                      - sum(k in [0, jL): A[i, k] * A[k, jL] )
                    ) / A[jL, jL]

        # --- U update: upper triangle including diagonal, row i, columns i .. N-1 ---
        # A[i, jU] = A[i, jU] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jU]
        # For fixed i, different jU iterations are independent.
        U(i, jU):
            for jU in [i, N):
                A[i, jU] =
                    A[i, jU]
                    - sum(k in [0, i): A[i, k] * A[k, jU])

dependencies:
    # The row loop i is explicitly sequential (seq), so rows execute in order:
    #   all updates for row i happen before row i+1.
    #
    # Within each row i:
    #   - L(i, jL) is sequential in jL by construction (seq).
    #   - U(i, jU) is independent across jU once all L(i, *) are known.
    #
    # To make this explicit:
    for i in [0, N), jL in [0, i), jU in [i, N):
        L(i, jL) -> U(i, jU)   # complete the L-part of row i before any U-part of row i

optimization:
    # High-level goals:
    #   - Respect all true data dependencies (no pivoting is introduced).
    #   - Keep the lower-triangular (L) jL-loop strictly sequential.
    #   - Turn the U-part into a cache-friendly, vectorized, and parallel update
    #     over the trailing submatrix.

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Reorder the U update to improve reuse (saxpy-like formulation)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # U(i, jU) currently computes:
    #   A[i, jU] = A[i, jU] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jU]
    # which is mathematically a reduction over k. The contributions from
    # different k are associative (up to FP round-off), so we can swap jU and k.
    #
    # Conceptual transformed order for the U-part at fixed i:
    #   for k in [0, i):
    #       let aik = A[i, k]    # hoist to a scalar
    #       for jU in [i, N):
    #           A[i, jU] -= aik * A[k, jU]
    #
    # This:
    #   - keeps A[i, k] (aik) in a register across many jU,
    #   - streams A[k, jU] and A[i, jU] in contiguous row-major order,
    #   - preserves the mathematical result.
    #
    # We express this via an interchange of jU and k in the U reduction.
    # (L's use of k is unchanged.)
    interchange(jU, k)  # applied only where jU and k are both active, effectively in U

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Tiling / blocking of U’s jU and k dimensions
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # After reordering, U’s effective structure per row i is:
    #   for k in [0, i):
    #     for jU in [i, N):
    #       A[i, jU] -= A[i, k] * A[k, jU]
    #
    # We tile jU and k to form cache-sized blocks over the trailing submatrix.
    # TJ and TK are tunable tile sizes that should be chosen to fit L1/L2.
    block(jU, JU, TJ)   # tile the trailing columns for better spatial locality
    block(k,  K,  TK)   # tile the reduction dimension to improve reuse of A[k, *]

    # Place tile loops just inside i to expose parallelism and maximize reuse
    hoist(JU)
    hoist(K)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Vectorization and parallelization of U over columns
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # After tiling, a typical inner kernel for U has shape:
    #   for K in tiles of k:
    #     for JU in tiles of jU:
    #       for k in K:
    #         aik = A[i, k]
    #         for jU in JU:
    #           A[i, jU] -= aik * A[k, jU]
    #
    # The innermost jU loop touches contiguous elements of A[i, jU] and A[k, jU],
    # so it is ideal for SIMD vectorization.
    vectorize(JU, VJ)   # VJ chosen per SIMD width (e.g., 4 or 8 doubles)

    # For fixed i, iterations over tiles JU are independent (no write conflicts),
    # so we can parallelize them across threads. The i loop itself remains
    # strictly sequential to respect the LU dependencies across rows.
    parallelize(JU)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Micro-optimizations for U’s reduction over k
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within each K tile, unroll the k-loop and keep A[i, k] in registers.
    # This reduces loop overhead and lets the compiler schedule FMAs efficiently.
    unroll(K, UK)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Local optimizations for the L update (lower triangle)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # L(i, jL) has an inner sum:
    #   sum_{k=0}^{jL-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jL]
    # which:
    #   - cannot reorder jL (data dependence along jL),
    #   - *can* tile/unroll k for slightly better cache behavior and ILP.
    #
    # We apply a modest tile of k (TK_L) and unroll that tile. The jL loop
    # itself remains 'seq' and is not parallelized or interchanged.
    block(k,  KL, TK_L)  # within L’s sum only; TK_L kept relatively small
    unroll(KL, UK_L)

    # NOTE:
    # - No additional large buffers are introduced; all updates are in-place on A.
    # - Extra storage, if any, is limited to a few scalars and small tiles
    #   implied by unrolling, well within the 50% memory-usage constraint.

    #  - diagonal and upper triangle (j >= i) hold U(i, j)

    # Reciprocal of diagonal pivots 1 / A[j, j]; used to avoid repeated divisions.

    # In-place, no-pivot LU factorization of A.
    # L has unit diagonal; its strictly lower part is stored in A[i, j] for j < i.
    # U is stored in the upper triangle of A, including the diagonal.

    for i in seq(0, N):              # outer loop over rows is strictly sequential

        # ---- 1. Compute strict lower-triangular entries L(i, j), 0 <= j < i ----
        #      L(i, j) = ( A(i, j) - sum_{k=0..j-1} L(i, k) * U(k, j) ) / U(j, j)
        #      We use inv_diag[j] = 1 / U(j, j) to replace division by multiplication.
        for j in seq(0, i):          # j ranges [0, i)

            A[i, j] =
                ( A[i, j]
                  - sum(k in [0, j): A[i, k] * A[k, j] )
                ) * inv_diag[j]

        # ---- 2. Compute upper-triangular row U(i, j), i <= j < N ----
        #      U(i, j) = A(i, j) - sum_{k=0..i-1} L(i, k) * U(k, j)
        for j in [i, N):
            U_update:
            A[i, j] =
                A[i, j]
                - sum(k in [0, i): A[i, k] * A[k, j])

        # ---- 3. Cache reciprocal of the new pivot for use in later rows ----
        # inv_diag[i] is used in L_update(row, j = i) for all row > i.
        DIAG_RECIP:
        inv_diag[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

    # ============================================================

    # ============================================================

    hoist(i)

    unroll(k, 4)

    # 1. 2D blocking in (k, j) to improve locality:

    #       for k in K:
    #         for j in J:
    #           A[i, j] -= A[i, k] * A[k, j]

    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    # ============================================================

domain:
    # Global iteration space (upper bounds are compile-time constant N)
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Single dense matrix, stored row-major, updated in-place.
    # On input: arbitrary SPD matrix A.
    # On output: in-place LU factorization without pivoting:
    #   - L has unit diagonal and is stored in the strict lower triangle of A.
    #   - U is stored in the diagonal and upper triangle of A.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

parameters:
    # Problem size (matches PolyBench's N and _PB_N)
    N: int

    # Tuning parameters for performance (not affecting correctness)
    TJ: int  # tile size for column dimension in upper update, e.g., 64
    UK: int  # unroll factor for inner products over k, e.g., 4
    VLEN: int  # SIMD width (number of DATA_TYPE lanes), e.g., 4 or 8

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # This is a Doolittle-like algorithm:
    #   For each row i:
    #     1) Compute L[i, 0..i-1] (strict lower part of row i).
    #     2) Compute U[i, i..N-1] (diagonal and upper part of row i).
    #
    # The original C code:
    #   for (i)
    #     for (j < i) { for (k < j) A[i][j] -= A[i][k]*A[k][j]; A[i][j] /= A[j][j]; }
    #     for (j >= i) for (k < i) A[i][j] -= A[i][k]*A[k][j];

    for i in seq([0, N)):                # outer loop must be sequential (row-to-row dependence)

        # 1) Compute strict lower part of row i: L(i, j) for j < i.
        #    Each A[i, j] is updated as:
        #       A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - sum_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i, k] * A[k, j]) / A[j, j]
        #    Note that A[i, k] for k < j are entries of L in row i, so j must be
        #    processed in increasing order (loop-carried dependence on row i).
        for j in seq([0, i)):
            A[i, j] =
                ( A[i, j]
                  - sum(k in [0, j), A[i, k] * A[k, j]) )
                / A[j, j]

        # 2) Compute diagonal and upper part of row i: U(i, j) for j >= i.
        #    Each A[i, j] is updated as:
        #       A[i, j] = A[i, j] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[k, j]
        #    All A[i, k] with k < i are now fixed (L row i is complete), and all
        #    A[k, j] with k < i, j >= i are from previously computed rows.
        #    Therefore, for fixed i:
        #      - different columns j in [i, N) are independent,
        #      - the sum over k is a pure reduction for each (i, j).
        for j in [i, N):
            A[i, j] =
                A[i, j]
                - sum(k in [0, i), A[i, k] * A[k, j])

dependencies:
    # Row dependencies:
    #   All computations at row i depend on rows 0..i-1.
    #   This enforces that i must be executed sequentially.
    for i in [1, N), j in [0, N):
        (all computations producing A[i-1, *]) -> (all computations using A[0..i-1, j] at row i)

    # Within-row, lower-part (L) dependencies:
    #   For fixed i, L(i, j) depends on previously computed entries in the same row i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [1, i), k in [0, j):
        A[i, k] -> A[i, j]   # j-loop in the lower update must be sequential

    # Within-row, upper-part (U) dependencies:
    #   For fixed i, U(i, j) for different j in [i, N) are independent:
    #     - They only share read-only data A[i, 0..i-1] and A[0..i-1, *].
    #     - No write-after-write or read-after-write between (i, j1) and (i, j2).
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [i, N), j2 in [i, N), j1 != j2:
        # No dependence between (i, j1) and (i, j2); they form a parallel set.
        (A[i, j1] update) --||-- (A[i, j2] update)

optimization:
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # High-level remarks:
    #   - The i-loop is inherently sequential because row i uses rows < i.
    #   - The lower-triangular loop over j (j < i) is also sequential because
    #     L(i, j) uses previously computed L(i, k) with k < j.
    #   - The upper-triangular loop (j >= i) has no loop-carried dependencies
    #     in j and is the dominant cost (~O(N^3/2) FLOPs). We exploit this
    #     for parallelism and vectorization.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1. Improve data locality and expose parallelism in the upper (U) update.
    #
    # We tile the j-dimension only for the upper-part update, then parallelize
    # tiles. This maintains the original evaluation order for the reduction over k
    # (we do not interchange j and k), therefore preserving C’s semantics for
    # each dot product A[i, j] −= sum_k A[i, k]*A[k, j].

    # block(j, JU, TJ) conceptually transforms:
    #   for j in [i, N):
    #       ...
    # into:
    #   for JU in [i, N) step TJ:
    #       for j in [JU, min(JU+TJ, N)):
    #           ...
    #
    # It is applied only to the "upper" j-loop.
    block(j /* in upper update */, JU, TJ)

    # Move the tile loop JU directly under i to make the parallel work chunks
    # coarser-grained and cache-friendly.
    hoist(JU)

    # Parallelize tiles of columns in the upper update.
    # For a given row i:
    #   - Different JU tiles cover disjoint column ranges.
    #   - There are no dependencies between tiles.
    #   - Each thread processes several adjacent columns, improving spatial locality.
    parallelize(JU)

    # Within a tile, encourage SIMD vectorization in the column dimension j.
    # This lets the compiler apply vector loads/stores for A[i, j] and A[k, j]
    # across nearby columns, even though the inner reduction is over k.
    vectorize(j, VLEN)

    # 2. Make inner products over k efficient in both L and U updates.
    #
    # The reductions over k in:
    #   sum(k in [0, j), ...)   and   sum(k in [0, i), ...)
    # are short-to-moderate-length dot products along the k-dimension.
    # We unroll and vectorize k to extract ILP and exploit SIMD where possible.
    #
    # Note: accesses A[i, k] are contiguous within a row; A[k, j] is strided by N.
    # Unrolling helps hide the latency of these strided loads.

    # Apply to both lower and upper k-reductions:
    unroll(k, UK)
    vectorize(k, VLEN)

    # 3. (Optional) Mild i-blocking for better cache behavior.
    #
    # This does *not* introduce parallelism (i-blocks must still execute in order)
    # but can reduce working-set size for large N by grouping nearby rows.
    # The transformation is:
    #   for i in [0, N):
    # into:
    #   for I in [0, N) step TI:
    #     for i in [I, min(I+TI, N)):
    #       ...
    #
    # TI is chosen so that the active part of rows 0..i and columns around i
    # fit better in caches on the target machine.
    # This is semantics-preserving because the internal order of i is unchanged.
    #
    # If desired, enable with a suitable TI (not shown as a parameter above):
    #   block(i, I, TI)
    #   hoist(I)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Memory-usage considerations:
    #   - No additional O(N^2) data structures are introduced; A remains the
    #     only N×N array.
    #   - Extra storage is limited to scalar temporaries and small vector
    #     registers (implied by sum/unroll/vectorize), keeping additional
    #     memory well below the allowed +50% over the original footprint.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  /* not necessary for LU, but using same code as cholesky */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_lu[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
	       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j, k;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <i; j++) {
       for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
          A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
        A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
    }
   for (j = i; j < _PB_N; j++) {
       for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
          A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
    }
  }
#pragma endscop
}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_lu (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

  return 0;
}

    parallelize(J_lu)

    vectorize(j, VECW)

domain:
    # Matrix is N x N, 0-based as in the C code
    i:  dim in [0, N)      # row index
    jL: dim in [0, N)      # column index for L-part (j < i)
    jU: dim in [0, N)      # column index for U-part (j >= i)
    k:  dim in [0, N)      # reduction / inner-product index

data:
    # In-place LU factors, stored in a single row-major array:
    #   - strict lower triangle (i > j): L (unit diagonal implied)
    #   - upper triangle (i <= j): U
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major layout

parameters:
    N: int                    # problem size
    # Tuning knobs for performance (compile-time or run-time constants):
    TJ: int                   # tile size for jU (columns of trailing submatrix), e.g., 64–256
    TK: int                   # tile size for k in U-part, e.g., 16–64
    TK_L: int                 # tile size for k in L-part, typically smaller than TK
    VJ: int                   # SIMD width used for vectorizing over columns (jU)
    UK: int                   # unroll factor for K in U-part
    UK_L: int                 # unroll factor for K in L-part

computation:
    # For each row i, first compute L(i, j) for j < i, then U(i, j) for j >= i.
    # This matches the original kernel_lu loop nest structurally.

    for i in seq([0, N)):

        # --- L update: strict lower triangle, row i, columns 0 .. i-1 ---
        # A[i, jL] = ( A[i, jL] - sum_{k=0}^{jL-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jL] ) / A[jL, jL]
        # jL must be processed in increasing order because A[i, k] for k < jL
        # are produced by earlier jL iterations.
        L(i, jL):
            for jL in seq([0, i)):
                A[i, jL] =
                    ( A[i, jL]
                      - sum(k in [0, jL): A[i, k] * A[k, jL] )
                    ) / A[jL, jL]

        # --- U update: upper triangle including diagonal, row i, columns i .. N-1 ---
        # A[i, jU] = A[i, jU] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jU]
        # For fixed i, different jU iterations are independent.
        U(i, jU):
            for jU in [i, N):
                A[i, jU] =
                    A[i, jU]
                    - sum(k in [0, i): A[i, k] * A[k, jU])

dependencies:
    # The row loop i is explicitly sequential (seq), so rows execute in order:
    #   all updates for row i happen before row i+1.
    #
    # Within each row i:
    #   - L(i, jL) is sequential in jL by construction (seq).
    #   - U(i, jU) is independent across jU once all L(i, *) are known.
    #
    # To make this explicit:
    for i in [0, N), jL in [0, i), jU in [i, N):
        L(i, jL) -> U(i, jU)   # complete the L-part of row i before any U-part of row i

optimization:
    # High-level goals:
    #   - Respect all true data dependencies (no pivoting is introduced).
    #   - Keep the lower-triangular (L) jL-loop strictly sequential.
    #   - Turn the U-part into a cache-friendly, vectorized, and parallel update
    #     over the trailing submatrix.

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Reorder the U update to improve reuse (saxpy-like formulation)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # U(i, jU) currently computes:
    #   A[i, jU] = A[i, jU] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jU]
    # which is mathematically a reduction over k. The contributions from
    # different k are associative (up to FP round-off), so we can swap jU and k.
    #
    # Conceptual transformed order for the U-part at fixed i:
    #   for k in [0, i):
    #       let aik = A[i, k]    # hoist to a scalar
    #       for jU in [i, N):
    #           A[i, jU] -= aik * A[k, jU]
    #
    # This:
    #   - keeps A[i, k] (aik) in a register across many jU,
    #   - streams A[k, jU] and A[i, jU] in contiguous row-major order,
    #   - preserves the mathematical result.
    #
    # We express this via an interchange of jU and k in the U reduction.
    # (L's use of k is unchanged.)
    interchange(jU, k)  # applied only where jU and k are both active, effectively in U

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Tiling / blocking of U’s jU and k dimensions
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # After reordering, U’s effective structure per row i is:
    #   for k in [0, i):
    #     for jU in [i, N):
    #       A[i, jU] -= A[i, k] * A[k, jU]
    #
    # We tile jU and k to form cache-sized blocks over the trailing submatrix.
    # TJ and TK are tunable tile sizes that should be chosen to fit L1/L2.
    block(jU, JU, TJ)   # tile the trailing columns for better spatial locality
    block(k,  K,  TK)   # tile the reduction dimension to improve reuse of A[k, *]

    # Place tile loops just inside i to expose parallelism and maximize reuse
    hoist(JU)
    hoist(K)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Vectorization and parallelization of U over columns
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # After tiling, a typical inner kernel for U has shape:
    #   for K in tiles of k:
    #     for JU in tiles of jU:
    #       for k in K:
    #         aik = A[i, k]
    #         for jU in JU:
    #           A[i, jU] -= aik * A[k, jU]
    #
    # The innermost jU loop touches contiguous elements of A[i, jU] and A[k, jU],
    # so it is ideal for SIMD vectorization.
    vectorize(JU, VJ)   # VJ chosen per SIMD width (e.g., 4 or 8 doubles)

    # For fixed i, iterations over tiles JU are independent (no write conflicts),
    # so we can parallelize them across threads. The i loop itself remains
    # strictly sequential to respect the LU dependencies across rows.
    parallelize(JU)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Micro-optimizations for U’s reduction over k
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within each K tile, unroll the k-loop and keep A[i, k] in registers.
    # This reduces loop overhead and lets the compiler schedule FMAs efficiently.
    unroll(K, UK)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Local optimizations for the L update (lower triangle)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # L(i, jL) has an inner sum:
    #   sum_{k=0}^{jL-1} A[i, k] * A[k, jL]
    # which:
    #   - cannot reorder jL (data dependence along jL),
    #   - *can* tile/unroll k for slightly better cache behavior and ILP.
    #
    # We apply a modest tile of k (TK_L) and unroll that tile. The jL loop
    # itself remains 'seq' and is not parallelized or interchanged.
    block(k,  KL, TK_L)  # within L’s sum only; TK_L kept relatively small
    unroll(KL, UK_L)

    # NOTE:
    # - No additional large buffers are introduced; all updates are in-place on A.
    # - Extra storage, if any, is limited to a few scalars and small tiles
    #   implied by unrolling, well within the 50% memory-usage constraint.

    # Reciprocal of diagonal pivots 1 / A[j, j]; used to avoid repeated divisions.
    inv_diag[j]: aux DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j   # contiguous 1D array

    # In-place, no-pivot LU factorization of A.

        #      L(i, j) = ( A(i, j) - sum_{k=0..j-1} L(i, k) * U(k, j) ) / U(j, j)

        for j in seq(0, i):          # j ranges [0, i)

                ( A[i, j]
                  - sum(k in [0, j): A[i, k] * A[k, j] )
                ) * inv_diag[j]

        # ---- 2. Compute upper-triangular row U(i, j), i <= j < N ----
        #      U(i, j) = A(i, j) - sum_{k=0..i-1} L(i, k) * U(k, j)
        for j in [i, N):
            U_update:
            A[i, j] =
                A[i, j]
                - sum(k in [0, i): A[i, k] * A[k, j])

        # ---- 3. Cache reciprocal of the new pivot for use in later rows ----

    # 1. Within a given row i, lower-factor entries L(i, j) must be computed

    # 2. Upper-factor entries U(i, j) on row i depend on the complete set of
    #    L(i, 0..i-1) multipliers of the same row.
    for i in [0, N), j in [i, N), k in [0, i):

    for i in [0, N):

optimization:
    # ============================================================
    # Global structure
    # ============================================================

    hoist(i)

    unroll(k, 4)

    #     for J in tiles of j in [i, N):

    unroll(k, 4)

domain:
    # Global iteration space (upper bounds are compile-time constant N)
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Single dense matrix, stored row-major, updated in-place.
    # On input: arbitrary SPD matrix A.
    # On output: in-place LU factorization without pivoting:
    #   - L has unit diagonal and is stored in the strict lower triangle of A.
    #   - U is stored in the diagonal and upper triangle of A.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

parameters:
    # Problem size (matches PolyBench's N and _PB_N)
    N: int

    # Tuning parameters for performance (not affecting correctness)
    TJ: int  # tile size for column dimension in upper update, e.g., 64
    UK: int  # unroll factor for inner products over k, e.g., 4
    VLEN: int  # SIMD width (number of DATA_TYPE lanes), e.g., 4 or 8

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # This is a Doolittle-like algorithm:
    #   For each row i:
    #     1) Compute L[i, 0..i-1] (strict lower part of row i).
    #     2) Compute U[i, i..N-1] (diagonal and upper part of row i).
    #
    # The original C code:
    #   for (i)
    #     for (j < i) { for (k < j) A[i][j] -= A[i][k]*A[k][j]; A[i][j] /= A[j][j]; }
    #     for (j >= i) for (k < i) A[i][j] -= A[i][k]*A[k][j];

    for i in seq([0, N)):                # outer loop must be sequential (row-to-row dependence)

        # 1) Compute strict lower part of row i: L(i, j) for j < i.
        #    Each A[i, j] is updated as:
        #       A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - sum_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i, k] * A[k, j]) / A[j, j]
        #    Note that A[i, k] for k < j are entries of L in row i, so j must be
        #    processed in increasing order (loop-carried dependence on row i).
        for j in seq([0, i)):
            A[i, j] =
                ( A[i, j]
                  - sum(k in [0, j), A[i, k] * A[k, j]) )
                / A[j, j]

        # 2) Compute diagonal and upper part of row i: U(i, j) for j >= i.
        #    Each A[i, j] is updated as:
        #       A[i, j] = A[i, j] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[k, j]
        #    All A[i, k] with k < i are now fixed (L row i is complete), and all
        #    A[k, j] with k < i, j >= i are from previously computed rows.
        #    Therefore, for fixed i:
        #      - different columns j in [i, N) are independent,
        #      - the sum over k is a pure reduction for each (i, j).
        for j in [i, N):
            A[i, j] =
                A[i, j]
                - sum(k in [0, i), A[i, k] * A[k, j])

dependencies:
    # Row dependencies:
    #   All computations at row i depend on rows 0..i-1.
    #   This enforces that i must be executed sequentially.
    for i in [1, N), j in [0, N):
        (all computations producing A[i-1, *]) -> (all computations using A[0..i-1, j] at row i)

    # Within-row, lower-part (L) dependencies:
    #   For fixed i, L(i, j) depends on previously computed entries in the same row i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [1, i), k in [0, j):
        A[i, k] -> A[i, j]   # j-loop in the lower update must be sequential

    # Within-row, upper-part (U) dependencies:
    #   For fixed i, U(i, j) for different j in [i, N) are independent:
    #     - They only share read-only data A[i, 0..i-1] and A[0..i-1, *].
    #     - No write-after-write or read-after-write between (i, j1) and (i, j2).
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [i, N), j2 in [i, N), j1 != j2:
        # No dependence between (i, j1) and (i, j2); they form a parallel set.
        (A[i, j1] update) --||-- (A[i, j2] update)

optimization:
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # High-level remarks:
    #   - The i-loop is inherently sequential because row i uses rows < i.
    #   - The lower-triangular loop over j (j < i) is also sequential because
    #     L(i, j) uses previously computed L(i, k) with k < j.
    #   - The upper-triangular loop (j >= i) has no loop-carried dependencies
    #     in j and is the dominant cost (~O(N^3/2) FLOPs). We exploit this
    #     for parallelism and vectorization.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1. Improve data locality and expose parallelism in the upper (U) update.
    #
    # We tile the j-dimension only for the upper-part update, then parallelize
    # tiles. This maintains the original evaluation order for the reduction over k
    # (we do not interchange j and k), therefore preserving C’s semantics for
    # each dot product A[i, j] −= sum_k A[i, k]*A[k, j].

    # block(j, JU, TJ) conceptually transforms:
    #   for j in [i, N):
    #       ...
    # into:
    #   for JU in [i, N) step TJ:
    #       for j in [JU, min(JU+TJ, N)):
    #           ...
    #
    # It is applied only to the "upper" j-loop.
    block(j /* in upper update */, JU, TJ)

    # Move the tile loop JU directly under i to make the parallel work chunks
    # coarser-grained and cache-friendly.
    hoist(JU)

    # Parallelize tiles of columns in the upper update.
    # For a given row i:
    #   - Different JU tiles cover disjoint column ranges.
    #   - There are no dependencies between tiles.
    #   - Each thread processes several adjacent columns, improving spatial locality.
    parallelize(JU)

    # Within a tile, encourage SIMD vectorization in the column dimension j.
    # This lets the compiler apply vector loads/stores for A[i, j] and A[k, j]
    # across nearby columns, even though the inner reduction is over k.
    vectorize(j, VLEN)

    # 2. Make inner products over k efficient in both L and U updates.
    #
    # The reductions over k in:
    #   sum(k in [0, j), ...)   and   sum(k in [0, i), ...)
    # are short-to-moderate-length dot products along the k-dimension.
    # We unroll and vectorize k to extract ILP and exploit SIMD where possible.
    #
    # Note: accesses A[i, k] are contiguous within a row; A[k, j] is strided by N.
    # Unrolling helps hide the latency of these strided loads.

    # Apply to both lower and upper k-reductions:
    unroll(k, UK)
    vectorize(k, VLEN)

    # 3. (Optional) Mild i-blocking for better cache behavior.
    #
    # This does *not* introduce parallelism (i-blocks must still execute in order)
    # but can reduce working-set size for large N by grouping nearby rows.
    # The transformation is:
    #   for i in [0, N):
    # into:
    #   for I in [0, N) step TI:
    #     for i in [I, min(I+TI, N)):
    #       ...
    #
    # TI is chosen so that the active part of rows 0..i and columns around i
    # fit better in caches on the target machine.
    # This is semantics-preserving because the internal order of i is unchanged.
    #
    # If desired, enable with a suitable TI (not shown as a parameter above):
    #   block(i, I, TI)
    #   hoist(I)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Memory-usage considerations:
    #   - No additional O(N^2) data structures are introduced; A remains the
    #     only N×N array.
    #   - Extra storage is limited to scalar temporaries and small vector
    #     registers (implied by sum/unroll/vectorize), keeping additional
    #     memory well below the allowed +50% over the original footprint.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  /* not necessary for LU, but using same code as cholesky */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}

void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_lu[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
	       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j, k;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <i; j++) {
       for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
          A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
        A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
    }
   for (j = i; j < _PB_N; j++) {
       for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
          A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
    }
  }
#pragma endscop
}

  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

    j: dim in [0, N)

    # On input: arbitrary SPD matrix A.
    # On output: in-place LU factorization without pivoting:
    #   - L has unit diagonal and is stored in the strict lower triangle of A.
    #   - U is stored in the diagonal and upper triangle of A.

    # Problem size (matches PolyBench's N and _PB_N)
    N: int

    # Tuning parameters for performance (not affecting correctness)
    TJ: int  # tile size for column dimension in upper update, e.g., 64
    UK: int  # unroll factor for inner products over k, e.g., 4
    VLEN: int  # SIMD width (number of DATA_TYPE lanes), e.g., 4 or 8

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # This is a Doolittle-like algorithm:
    #   For each row i:
    #     1) Compute L[i, 0..i-1] (strict lower part of row i).
    #     2) Compute U[i, i..N-1] (diagonal and upper part of row i).
    #
    # The original C code:
    #   for (i)
    #     for (j < i) { for (k < j) A[i][j] -= A[i][k]*A[k][j]; A[i][j] /= A[j][j]; }
    #     for (j >= i) for (k < i) A[i][j] -= A[i][k]*A[k][j];

    for i in seq([0, N)):                # outer loop must be sequential (row-to-row dependence)

        # 1) Compute strict lower part of row i: L(i, j) for j < i.
        #    Each A[i, j] is updated as:
        #       A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - sum_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i, k] * A[k, j]) / A[j, j]
        #    Note that A[i, k] for k < j are entries of L in row i, so j must be
        #    processed in increasing order (loop-carried dependence on row i).
        for j in seq([0, i)):
            A[i, j] =
                ( A[i, j]
                  - sum(k in [0, j), A[i, k] * A[k, j]) )
                / A[j, j]

        # 2) Compute diagonal and upper part of row i: U(i, j) for j >= i.
        #    Each A[i, j] is updated as:
        #       A[i, j] = A[i, j] - sum_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[k, j]
        #    All A[i, k] with k < i are now fixed (L row i is complete), and all
        #    A[k, j] with k < i, j >= i are from previously computed rows.

        #      - the sum over k is a pure reduction for each (i, j).

                - sum(k in [0, i), A[i, k] * A[k, j])

    # Row dependencies:
    #   All computations at row i depend on rows 0..i-1.
    #   This enforces that i must be executed sequentially.

    #   For fixed i, L(i, j) depends on previously computed entries in the same row i.

    #   - The i-loop is inherently sequential because row i uses rows < i.
    #   - The lower-triangular loop over j (j < i) is also sequential because
    #     L(i, j) uses previously computed L(i, k) with k < j.
    #   - The upper-triangular loop (j >= i) has no loop-carried dependencies

    # We tile the j-dimension only for the upper-part update, then parallelize

    # (we do not interchange j and k), therefore preserving C’s semantics for

    #   for JU in [i, N) step TJ:

    vectorize(j, VLEN)

    # We unroll and vectorize k to extract ILP and exploit SIMD where possible.

    vectorize(k, VLEN)

    # but can reduce working-set size for large N by grouping nearby rows.
    # The transformation is:

    # into:
    #   for I in [0, N) step TI:
    #     for i in [I, min(I+TI, N)):
    #       ...

    #   hoist(I)

/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  /* not necessary for LU, but using same code as cholesky */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_lu[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
	       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j, k;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <i; j++) {
       for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
          A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
        A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
    }
   for (j = i; j < _PB_N; j++) {
       for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
          A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
    }
  }
#pragma endscop
}

{

  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_lu (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed

  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

  return 0;
}
